correctness.rationale: Finite expected absorption follows from a uniform no-reset exit chance. The entire even-power series solves the exact killed backward equation termwise and matches both absorbing boundaries. Bounded-solution uniqueness follows by the stopped generator. The packaged numerical solver passed 93 separate tests; proof does not depend on these finite checks.

originality.rationale: The reviewed primary articles treat either a fixed proportional factor with a one-sided target, fixed-location resets with two boundaries, or state-independent random reset locations. Their statements and displayed general backward equations do not assert sharp optimization over all random multiplicative-factor laws at fixed quadratic retention. The current theorem supplies necessary and sufficient equality classes, a variance-preserving search-time separation, and its asymptotic rate. Prior single-factor recurrences and convex moment inequalities are acknowledged; literature priority is qualified by residual risks.
residual_risks: An unlocated general comparison theorem for positive-kernel nonlocal Dirichlet equations may subsume the sharp factor-law inequality.
Published work not indexed in the checked sources may treat random rescaling multipliers and symmetric absorption.
The reviewed statement concerns mathematical novelty of the law-level extrema, not novelty of the fixed-a recursion or ordinary Jensen inequality.

value.rationale: The fixed E[A^2] restriction fixes stationary positional variance for the unbounded searcher, creating a natural common-cost comparison. Despite identical stationary variance, mean symmetric exit has unique globally optimal reset-factor laws and an exponentially diverging fast-reset protocol ratio. This is a motivated exact protocol-design invariant not merely a new coefficient in a known table.
